sources.title: Human History Map: Bengal 1783 index and decoded geometry
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Exact missing ID bengal-1783; one world1783 polygon, map interval1783-1800, bounds82.60-92.60E and21.00-27.54N. The outline includes territory beyond the Bengal delta and disappears in the 1800 snapshot even though Company rule continued.

sources.title: Sirajul Islam, Colonial Period, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh synthesis directly read. 1765 diwani, Permanent Settlement, export and artisan changes. Value judgments about entire social classes are not repeated; policy structure and broad economic change are used cautiously.

sources.title: Sirajul Islam, Diwani, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh institutional history directly read. Mughal diwani structure, imperial farman of12August1765 and Company revenue role in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. It supports legal chronology without implying that the Mughal emperor exercised day-to-day control.

sources.title: UK Parliament: East India Company and Raj, 1785-1858
sources.note: Official parliamentary history directly read. Company expansion after1798 and loss of administrative power in1858. Used only for continuation beyond the atlas seam; the page’s imperial framing is not adopted as a moral judgment.

sources.title: Sirajul Islam, Administration, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh synthesis directly read. Revenue experiments, Pitt’s India Act, Cornwallis Code, courts and 1793 local-government changes. Typographic OCR errors silently normalized.

sources.title: S. Aminul Islam, Social Stratification, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh synthesis directly read. Rural agrarian majority, zamindars, cultivators and stratification. No religion or caste is assigned a single experience.

sources.title: Sirajul Islam, Sarraf, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh article directly read. Coin exchange, bills, collectorate work and 1793 revenue payments. Contemporaries’ suspicions are described as prejudice, not adopted as fact.

sources.title: Printing, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh article directly read. Wilkins’s Hooghly press, Panchanan Karmakar’s type-making skill and 1778 grammar. Later linotype history omitted.

sources.title: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed, A Grammar of the Bengal Language (1778)
sources.note: Public-domain scan of original Hoogly printing directly consulted with catalogue corroboration. Vowel sample is modern Unicode transcription of the printed forms; modern romanization is not Halhed’s phonetic system.

sources.title: The Bengali Character in Print and Writing, Archaeological Survey of India
sources.note: Public-domain institutional scan directly read. Gives modern transliteration of initial vowel forms অ a, আ ā, ই i, ঈ ī. Used only to explain the letter sample, grouped conceptually with the 1778 facsimile.

sources.title: A. M. A. Haque, Calcutta Madrasa, Banglapedia
sources.note: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh article directly read. 1780 founding, 1782 government takeover, head teachers and curriculum/employment purpose. It does not establish mass or girls’ schooling.

sources.title: The Asiatic Society, Kolkata: institutional history and library
sources.note: Institutional history directly read. 1784 manuscript gifts, later library opening and collection growth. Membership restrictions checked against the Society’s RTI history; no claim that it was an inclusive public academy in this period.

sources.title: D. G. Crawford, Notes on the Early Hospitals of Calcutta, Indian Medical Gazette (1903)
sources.note: Historical medical article scan directly read. General Native Hospital opening in1792 and an earlier 1789 proposal concerning servants of officers. The term used by the source is contextualized; access and treatment quality are not inferred.

sources.title: University of Texas, The Solvyns Project
sources.note: Academic digital project directly read. Complete 1796/1799 Calcutta etching series and publication history. The images are a European artist’s selective, sometimes prejudiced observations, not a census.

sources.title: Bhau Daji Lad Museum, Cotton Manufacture, Trade and Textiles
sources.note: Museum story directly read. Solvyns’s 1798/1799 weaver image and period commentary on looms, family labor and muslin; numerical citywide estimates omitted. Artist’s contemptuous generalizations are not adopted.

sources.title: Wellcome Collection: Market scene, Calcutta, 1799
sources.note: Institutional object record directly read. Original colored etching by Solvyns, Calcutta1799. Visual evidence supports a mixed open market and material setting, not exact prices or universal dress.

sources.title: Heritage Transport Museum: A Pansway, 1799
sources.note: Museum object record directly read. 1799 Calcutta etching, small passage boat used for inland river navigation. The description is specific to this boat type.

proposedOverrides.name: Bengal under East India Company rule
proposedOverrides.summary: Company-ruled Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in the atlas’s 1783-1800 snapshot, with farming, weaving, courts and markets continuing beyond the map seam.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported record is one 1783-1800 snapshot with bounds82.60-92.60E and21.00-27.54N; it is broader than the Bengal delta.
The label Bengal is publicly qualified as Company-ruled territory under the Mughal diwani framework, not an independent kingdom.
The 1800 disappearance is a map seam. Company rule continued and later atlas records use broader British East India Company labels.
